body:
[A10] READY SCOPE / IMPLEMENTATION DECISION

Select `hdl/common/axis_mux_rr_2in_1out.sv` as the first representative module. It is used by the existing `ptp_ts` regression and the timestamp datapath. At dev `88e9276b2a220c716f64a843f7e1eb8f9265e896`, first-party HDL/test sources contain no `assert property` or module `bind`, and the suite does not enable `--assert`. This task introduces an executable assertion example without changing product RTL behavior.

Authority and entry points: REQUIREMENTS REQ-VER-01/02/04; CONTRIBUTING sections 1, 2 and 3; CODE_QUALITY rules on contract checks and mutation-proven evidence; `tb/verilator/ptp_ts/{Makefile,sim_main.cpp}`, `tb/common/verilator_harness.hpp`, `scripts/suite_tally.py`, `scripts/run_all_suites.sh`; the mux's existing ready/valid, packet ownership and reset contract. [Arm IHI0051A section 2.2](https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/642583d7314e245d086bc8c9) defines the AXI-Stream handshake and stability obligation. [Pinned Verilator v5.050 language support](https://github.com/verilator/verilator/blob/v5.050/docs/guide/languages.rst) limits bind targets to module names and describes its mostly two-state simulation; [v5.050 invocation options](https://github.com/verilator/verilator/blob/v5.050/docs/guide/exe_verilator.rst) define assertion enablement. Verify behavior with that pinned executable, not only current documentation.

In scope:

- Add reusable, simulation-only AXI-Stream ready/valid stability assertions in a separate checker, bound by module name to the real mux. Check stalled valid persistence and stable data/keep/last, mutual exclusion of input grants, and legal mux state/packet ownership at clocked boundaries. State clearly which obligations belong to the stimulus and which to the DUT. Add immediate invariant checks where useful, without changing the synthesizable implementation.
- Integrate the bound checks into the existing `ptp_ts` default regression, preserving every original test. A small additional executable/wrapper within that suite may exercise the mux directly at 8-bit and 64-bit widths. Keep the existing suite owner, shard inventory and CI policy; no new workflow or global assertion flag change.
- Exercise both input ports, simultaneous offers, single/multiple beats, valid gaps, last-beat and multi-cycle backpressure, reset while stalled, release and resumed traffic. Require independent activity/antecedent witnesses so a disconnected checker or unused path is not a pass. A scoreboard must verify transfers and packet ordering independently of checker internals.
- Prove each newly claimed property is sensitive: bounded scratch DUT/stimulus mutations must build successfully, trigger the intended named assertion, and return nonzero. An assertion-disabled or missing-bind control must fail the campaign's expected-detection check. Retain raw negative logs separately; do not leak expected failures into the normal suite tally or count failed probes as passing DUT checks. Compilation failures, timeouts and unrelated aborts are not detection.
- Document how to add a checker, bind it, enable it, handle reset/past state, name a failure and reproduce positive/negative controls. Explicitly state that two-state simulation does not establish four-state X propagation, CDC correctness, timing closure, formal proof, or whole-product coverage. No functional covergroup rollout is included.

Frozen acceptance interpretation: the issue's three acceptance criteria are met by this bound representative module, independently detected injected faults, and the reusable guidelines. Product RTL, firmware, PP (protocol processor) and gPTP processor sources/pins, shipping bytes and behavior stay unchanged. New product defects discovered by the checks are published for a separate scoped decision; never weaken a property to keep the suite green.

Validation: `make -C tb/verilator/ptp_ts` passes with original tests plus the bound positive and detection-control campaign; `python3 scripts/suite_tally.py --verdict <captured-suite-log>` accepts the normal log; the ordinary full sweep must execute the new checks under the existing owner. Documentation, source-list/traceability, idiom, hygiene and ratchet gates pass without budget widening. Record exact commands, counts, mutation causes and pinned tool identity. The manager additionally runs the full local/native, trusted act, hosted, current-candidate and post-merge bars.

Executor A170 (Opus); independent cleared-context internal reviewer R239 (Opus) and external reviewer R240 (Codex); manager A10. The sole author slot is available after A169's completed #512 link correction. This test-only lane is disjoint from the frozen #437 parser, #464 AEM selftest and #478 rate-bound lanes; preserve the existing `ptp_ts` owner and avoid their shared CI files. Branch creation and Project In progress precede any edit. No hardware work or dependency adoption. No unresolved design choice remains for this bounded rollout.
